title.en: Trace a sequence of stack operations

say.en: With a stack you can only put something on top or take the top thing off. Those two moves are PUSH and POP. In this lesson: Perform PUSH and POP.
Explain overflow and underflow.
Trace a sequence of stack operations.

body.en: PUSH adds a new element at the TOP of the stack; it is an insertion. Adding to a stack that is already full is an exception called overflow. POP removes the topmost element; it is a deletion. Removing from an empty stack is called underflow. Other helpful *operations* are isEmpty, top (peek at the top element) and size.

points.en: PUSH: insert at TOP; full *stack* → overflow
POP: delete from TOP; empty *stack* → underflow
isEmpty, top (peek), size help to use a *stack* safely

title.en: On the board: Tracing PUSH and POP

say.en: Start empty and push 5, then 8, then 3. The TOP moves up each time.
POP removes and returns the top element, 3.
Push 9. Then peek, or top, shows 9 without removing it.
Popping an empty stack is underflow. Pushing onto a full stack is overflow. Check isEmpty before popping.

problem.en: Glasses are stacked one by one: PUSH glass1, PUSH glass2, POP, PUSH glass3, PUSH glass4, POP. Show the stack after each step.

steps.en: PUSH glass3, PUSH glass4 → [glass1, glass3, glass4]; POP removes glass4 → [glass1, glass3]

answer.en: Final stack (bottom to top): glass1, glass3; TOP = glass3

narration.en: Trace the stack after every operation. Remember that POP always takes the top element.

say.en: Trace the stack after every operation. Remember that POP always takes the top element. Glasses are stacked one by one: PUSH glass1, PUSH glass2, POP, PUSH glass3, PUSH glass4, POP. Show the stack after each step.
PUSH glass1 gives [glass1].
PUSH glass2 gives [glass1, glass2].
POP gives removes glass2 gives [glass1].
PUSH glass3, PUSH glass4 gives [glass1, glass3, glass4]; POP removes glass4 gives [glass1, glass3].
So the answer is Final stack bottom to top: glass1, glass3; TOP equals glass3.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 are pushed onto a stack in this order, and POPs may be done at any time in between. Which output sequence is NOT possible?
To pop 3 first, 1 and 2 must already be on the stack with 2 above 1, so 1 cannot come out before 2.
The other orders can all be produced.
